name: Khangchendzonga National Park
description: Khangchendzonga National Park covers about 1,784 square kilometres of northern Sikkim, India, rising from forested valleys and lakes to glaciers and snowfields. It is dominated by Kangchenjunga, the world's third-highest peak at 8,586 metres. Local people revere the mountain and its caves, rivers and lakes as sacred, and these beliefs blend with Buddhism. In 2016 it became India's first mixed natural and cultural World Heritage Site.
